description: 4072 Voice Core: the ARP 4072 low-pass filter, two envelopes and the 4019 amplifier, taking its audio from an oscillator

params.text: Sets the filter cutoff, 10Hz to 20000Hz
Sets the resonance, 0 to 100%
Sets the drive into the filter, -60dB to 24dB; fully down mutes the input
Scales how far the filter envelope moves the cutoff, -100 to +100%
Attenuverts the cutoff modulation input
Attenuverts the resonance modulation input
Sets the gain the amplifier holds with no control applied
Scales how far the amplifier envelope opens the amplifier
Scales the VCA modulation input
Sets the attack of the filter envelope, 1.4ms to 5 seconds
Sets the decay of the filter envelope, 6.4ms to 6 seconds
Sets the level the filter envelope holds while the gate stays high
Sets the release of the filter envelope, 0.52ms to 6 seconds
Chooses ADSR, AD or AR for the filter envelope
Changes the curvature of both envelopes without changing their stage times, -100 to +100%
Sets the attack of the amplifier envelope, 1.4ms to 5 seconds
Sets the decay of the amplifier envelope, 6.4ms to 6 seconds
Sets the level the amplifier envelope holds while the gate stays high
Sets the release of the amplifier envelope, 0.52ms to 6 seconds
Chooses ADSR, AD or AR for the amplifier envelope
Chooses whether a patched cutoff modulation adds to the filter envelope or replaces it, marked + and EXT
Chooses whether a patched VCA modulation adds to the amplifier envelope or replaces it, marked + and EXT
Reads the cutoff modulation as linear frequency at 200Hz per volt or as exponential pitch, marked LIN and EXP
Reads the VCA modulation as linear gain or as exponential gain, marked LIN and EXP
Reads the amplifier envelope as linear gain or as exponential gain, marked LIN and EXP

inputs.text: Audio into the amplifier in place of the filter output
Moves the cutoff, one octave per volt
Modulates the cutoff, scaled by its attenuverter
Modulates the resonance, scaled by its attenuverter
Modulates the amplifier gain, scaled by its knob
Starts and holds both envelopes; it rises at 1V and releases below 0.1V
Retriggers both envelopes at 1V; with nothing patched, the gate does the retriggering

outputs.text: The filtered audio, taken before the amplifier

notes: nothing comes out of the amplifier until a gate is patched: both envelopes rest at zero, and the amplifier is closed unless VCA INIT is raised
